text:
maria: heads-up — queue depth spike in eu-west-1 for redwood-7b-quant and open-llama-13b. 5m avg queue: redwood-7b-quant=480, open-llama-13b=320. p95 latency ~7.2s. dashboard: https://console.redwood/eu-west-1/queues?range=5m :grimacing:

infra-bot: alert triggered: queue_depth_high region=eu-west-1 model=redwood-7b-quant value=480 threshold=200

aj: ack. are nodes saturated or is this a routing blip?

orion: checking gpu pool eu-west-1-gpupool-3 — nodes at ~98% mem, ~92% compute. multiple pods showing small alloc failures but no OOMs. autoscaler didn't add nodes — we're at max nodes for that AZ/quota. cloud request pending. ETA to new nodes ~42m if quota approved.

keiko: ok. we should triage by applying temporary admission controls and fast-fail to protect latency. propose: set max_concurrency=64 for redwood-7b-quant, 48 for open-llama-13b in eu-west-1 and enable 429 for queue position >200 for non-SLA traffic. also enable prefix caching for common prompts.

maria: how do we flip the admission controls quickly?

keiko: use the internal admin API or rictl. example curl: 

```
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/admin/admission \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","model":"redwood-7b-quant","max_concurrency":64,"fast_fail_threshold":200}'
```

aj: i'll apply the redwood-7b-quant change and add the 429 rule for non-prod keys. flipping now.

aj: applied admission control for redwood-7b-quant => max_concurrency=64, fast_fail_threshold=200. open-llama-13b next.

orion: observed immediate effect: redwood-7b-quant queue dropped to ~260 within 3m, p95 latency decreased to ~3.1s. open-llama still 310.

sahil: i've opened a cloud quota ticket (CLOUD-REQ-8742) to increase GPUs in eu-west-1. asked for expedited review; estimated 48m if approved.

maria: routing question — can we route lower-priority eu-west-1 traffic to burst pool in us-west-2 as a short-term mitigation?

orion: technically yes via smart-routing policy, but user-perceived latency will increase for EU users; better option is to route low-priority to the quantized variant redwood-7b-q4a which lives in the same region. cheaper and lower memory.

keiko: let's do both: route non-SLA to q4a and set cross-region burst only for critical background jobs where latency is less sensitive. i'll push routing policy change.

aj: made routing change for non-SLA keys -> redwood-7b-q4a in eu-west-1. added temporary per-key rate limit: 20 requests/min for trial users.

orion: metrics 10m after changes: redwood-7b-quant queue ~180, open-llama ~220, overall cluster GPU util down from 96% to 88%. small tail still present but stable.

infra-bot: incident created INC-2026-332: "eu-west-1 queue saturation — admission controls applied, scaling in progress" assigned to eng-sre oncall.

maria: thanks. please add a follow-up: improve autoscaler to consider cross-AZ quotas and fallback to temporary admission control earlier. also add an alert to fire at queue depth >250 per-model per-region (not global).

keiko: noted — will add postmortem and action items. main takeaways: tighten autoscaler guardrails, add per-model regional alerts, and document emergency admission control runbook.

ops-oncall: monitoring for regressions. will reopen thread if anything spikes again. :white_check_mark:

maria: nice work team, keep me posted on quota approval and any regressions.
